comment: Dear Millcreek Council Person, I am writing to urge you not to approve tlie proposed additional digital billboards at the Millcreek City Center. I am not a fan of any billboards along orir roads and byways. They are such a blight to one's senses being constantly barraged by advertising that I do not want to see. The boards that hawk beauty makeovers and erectile disfunction are especially offensive. One of the reasons I love traveling, especially to other countries, is their lack of billboards and other advertisements that are unwanted by the population. I see the landscape and enjoy the people and sights and the natural beauty of the area. This is particularly true for the Salt Lake Valley and suburbs nestled beneath the grandeur of the Wasatch Front. I realize that this ship has long ago sailed, and I must learn to live with the visual and cultural damage. However, I believe it is not too late to stop spoiling the beautiful City of Millcreek. When I saw the current digital sign at the City Center my first thought was that of Las Vegas, Downtown Los Arigeles or Times Square, New York, with their garish digital signs and light shows. Please, may the Council be better than that. Let ris turn Millcreek City into a kinder and gentler city such as Boulder, CO, Stowe, Vermont, Carmel, CA. Please strive to be a City that values peace and tranquility over blatant liglitshow adveitising. At the very least, please press tlie pause button for a couple years and then evaluate the need and effects of digital signs. Once they are up, they will NEVER come down and more will be added. I also rinderstand that Digital Signs are a driver safety issue, but I will leave this issrie to others more knowledgeable. Thank you for your considersation. Brent Crane r
